convergence.iterationNotes: Iteration 1 (authoring from extracted normalized-prototype scene graphs; pen text placement from a calibration probe - pen centers Heebo's font bounding box [asc 1.048/desc 0.421] in the lineHeight box; y = baseline - 0.8135*fontSize at lineHeight 1) converged all 14 states at 0.05-0.82%. Iteration 2 probed a global text-baseline tune of +/-0.5px: +0.5 regressed everywhere; -0.5 improved HTML-derived text (config-error 0.82->0.28) but regressed SVG-derived text - the two baseline families carry different systematic offsets (Chromium integer-rounds font metrics per size for HTML line boxes; SVG baselines are exact). Iteration 3 split the tune (HTML-only -0.5 / -0.25): -0.25 best (mean 0.169%, max 0.36%). Iteration 4 probed HTML -0.375: regressed vs -0.25 - plateau; iteration 3's -0.25 stands as final. Post-convergence, one token-binding defect (focus ring bound sem-text-header instead of sem-borders-focus - same resolved light value, zero pixel delta) was corrected and the full check suite re-run. default==static-print and slice-hover==slice-pressed exports are byte-identical, matching the contract's identical-by-construction claims.

tokenJudgmentCalls.surface: categorical palette (all 15 --cat* variables; categorical-palette frame slice/swatch fills)
tokenJudgmentCalls.prototypeValue: Bill's blue-first ordering of the same 15 hues Hemlock owns (#3B82F6 first)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: Chart-series rule: bind chart-series roles in series order, never hue-match. Bill's set is the identical 15 hues in a different priority order, so the positional mapping deliberately reshuffles rendered hues (slice 0 purple #8951F0 instead of blue #3B82F6). The alternative (hue-matching each --catN to its Hemlock twin) would preserve Bill's pixels but scramble the priority semantics.

tokenJudgmentCalls.surface: ramp palette (shipped default; 7 hues x full + 60%-alpha strengths)
tokenJudgmentCalls.prototypeValue: blue #3A6AF8 / purple #8951F0 / green #148338 / pink #E73CAE / orange #FB923C / brown #92400E / charcoal #45423E, half-steps as rgba(...,0.6)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: Hemlock has no multi-hue ramp vocabulary (chart-sequential is single-hue blue; chart-categorical owns different roles). Created as a first-class chart-palette family with Bill's own dark values (the prototype ships a complete dark token set). 4 of 7 hues coincide with existing chart-categorical values (hue-02=color-01, hue-04=color-10, hue-05=color-13, hue-06=color-12) - noted for the designer's remap option. The -a60 companions carry TRUE alpha (#...99) per the v002 doctrine (design-rules 9): the half-steps composite over what is behind the chart. PENDING-P3 posture: alpha kept, not precomputed.

tokenJudgmentCalls.surface: focus dim (non-focused slices and legend rows in hover/press/focus states)
tokenJudgmentCalls.prototypeValue: runtime SVG opacity 0.28 (slices) / CSS opacity 0.4 (legend rows)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: v002 deliberately dims via runtime opacity (design-rules 9 - the opposite of v001's precomputed-solid doctrine; the dispatch template's anti-seam example is v001 text and does not govern v002). Carried as node opacity, the .pen-native equivalent, so a base-token swap re-derives the dimmed appearance for free. PENDING-P3 records the open designer question.

Bill paints the paired highlight blue - selection/highlight semantics, value-identical to the highlight role (blue-100). The v001 precedent (sem-background-rowHover, warm taupe) was considered and rejected: v002's row state is a paired SELECTION highlight, not a generic row hover, and binding rowHover would repaint it taupe.

Hemlock's a11y contract names sem-borders-focus as THE focus ring; role-first binding turns the ring near-black (#0E0E0E) in light. Deliberate divergence from the prototype's accent-blue ring (same call as the v001 capture).

tokenJudgmentCalls.surface: Legend switch (track on / track off / thumb)
tokenJudgmentCalls.prototypeValue: track on #3A6AF8, track off #B6B9B7, thumb #FFFFFF (iOS-style filled-track switch)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: Bill's switch idiom inverts Hemlock's ToggleSwitch (Hemlock: pale toggleTrackOn #EBF0FE + accent knob; Bill: accent track + white knob). Binding toggleTrackOn to Bill's track would break the coupled track/thumb contrast pair (white thumb on near-white track), so the on-track binds the T2 action role (value-identical) and the off-track adopts the toggleTrackOff role (repaint #B6B9B7 -> #EDEAE3, which is exactly Hemlock's own off design). The idiom divergence itself is recorded as a non-token design gap; composing the library ToggleSwitch was rejected because the geometry contract (36x20 track, 16px thumb at left 18/2) is probed against the prototype.

tokenJudgmentCalls.prototypeValue: feDropShadow dy3 std5 black@16%; 0 1px 2px black@5%; 0 8px 24px black@18%
tokenJudgmentCalls.boundToken: $y:prim-shadow-md-color + shadow-md-y/blur; $y:prim-shadow-sm-color + shadow-sm-y/blur; shadow-lg family (tip unreachable in contracted states)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: Hemlock chart rules pin floating-card shadows to shadow-md; the elevation family owns all shadows. Values repainted to the family's y/blur/alpha. NOTE - doc<->lib naming drift: the design-system doc and token guide name shadow colors 'shadow-{size}-color' (no prefix, 'semantic by nature... components may bind them directly'); the live hemlock-library.lib.pen carries them as 'prim-shadow-{size}-color'. They are themed light/dark pairs (functionally T2) and are the library's only shadow-color tokens, so the live names are bound directly and the drift is flagged for the design-system owner rather than minting shadow aliases.
